caption: Does the singular word “offspring” identify Jesus? In Genesis, the same word describes descendants as numerous as the stars. Singular grammar does not make it one person.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Does one “offspring” mean Jesus? God promises land to Abraham’s “offspring.” Paul later points out that the word is singular and says it refers to Christ.
slides.body: God promises land to Abraham’s “offspring.” Paul later points out that the word is singular and says it refers to Christ.
slides.heading: Does one “offspring” mean Jesus?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Gen 12:7: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, ‘I will give this land to your offspring.’
slides.body: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, ‘I will give this land to your offspring.’
slides.heading: Gen 12:7

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Gal 3:16, BSB: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.
slides.body: The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.
slides.heading: Claimed fulfilment · Gal 3:16

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Why Christians connect them Paul reads all God’s promises to Abraham as reaching their goal in one person: Jesus. People who belong to Jesus then become part of Abraham’s family too.
slides.body: Paul reads all God’s promises to Abraham as reaching their goal in one person: Jesus. People who belong to Jesus then become part of Abraham’s family too.
slides.heading: Why Christians connect them

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the word includes many people Genesis compares this same “offspring” to countless dust and stars. The word is singular but normally describes a whole family. Its grammar alone does not identify Jesus.
slides.body: Genesis compares this same “offspring” to countless dust and stars. The word is singular but normally describes a whole family. Its grammar alone does not identify Jesus.
slides.heading: But the word includes many people

title: Does ‘offspring’ secretly mean one person—Jesus?
